profile.summary: Nucleotide Transformer v3 (NTv3) is a family of DNA models from InstaDeep that read up to about 1 million bases at single-base resolution, across many species. Pre-trained checkpoints learn from unlabelled genomes by predicting masked bases and give embeddings. Post-trained checkpoints are further trained to predict functional genomics tracks (such as chromatin accessibility, histone marks and transcription factor binding) and genome annotations, given the species.
profile.summary_source_locator: docs/nucleotide_transformer_v3.md at commit 2dc37b86: opening, Model Variants and Sizes, How to Use

summary_quotes.text: NTv3 uses a **U-Net-like architecture** with **single-base tokenization**, enabling efficient processing of million-nucleotide contexts at nucleotide resolution.
Pre-trained models using masked language modeling on OpenGenome2 with context length ≤1 Mb:
Post-trained models extend pre-trained models with supervised objectives for functional tracks and genome annotations across 24 species:
**Functional tracks** (BigWig): ~16,000 tracks including chromatin accessibility, histone modifications, and transcription factor binding
Post-trained models require species conditioning and can predict functional tracks and genome annotations:

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: NTv3 is a U-Net. A convolutional tower shortens the single-base token sequence by 2 to the power of the number of downsampling blocks (128 for the main models, which have 7), a transformer processes the compressed sequence with self-attention, and a deconvolutional tower with skip connections restores single-base resolution. Pre-training uses masked language modelling on 9 trillion base pairs from OpenGenome2, with a length curriculum up to 1 Mb. Post-training adds supervised learning on about 16,000 functional tracks and annotation labels from 24 species, with adaptive layer norms for species conditioning. Post-trained track and annotation outputs cover the middle 37.5% of the input.
sections.source_locator: docs at commit 2dc37b86: Architecture, Training Overview, Ablations note, How to Use

quotes.text: **Convolutional downsampling tower:** Reduces sequence length by $2^n$ where $n$ = `num_downsamples` through convolutions
**Transformer core:** Processes the compressed representation with self-attention
**Deconvolutional upsampling tower:** Restores original sequence resolution with skip connections
For the main models, this is **128 for 7 downsamples**.
Trained on **9 trillion base pairs** from OpenGenome2 using base-resolution masked language modeling (MLM), scaling context to 1 Mb through a length curriculum and mixed-length training.
Joint objective integrating continued self-supervision with supervised learning on **~16,000 functional tracks** and annotation labels from **24 animal and plant species**.
**Species-conditioning:** Adaptive layer norms for multi-species support
# NOTE: The post-trained model crops bigwig and bed track outputs to the middle 37.5%

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The initial release (2025) has pre-trained models of 8M, 100M and 650M parameters and post-trained models of 100M and 650M, plus intermediate checkpoints (8kb and 131kb stages) and experimental 5-downsample models of 592M. Each repository is tagged v1.0. These checkpoints need the code at commit 2dc37b8. InstaDeep has since released a second generation (NTv3_pretrained, NTv3_tracks, NTv3_tracks_1mb, NTv3_annot_mammals, _plants, _insects) with a different architecture, which the current code loads instead; the initial-release checkpoints are unchanged and still published. A result should name the checkpoint, the revision or v1.0 tag, and the code commit; this page read NTv3_100M_post at revision 28cb2afa.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Multi-species genomic foundation model: masked language model (pre-trained) with supervised track and annotation heads (post-trained).

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: U-Net: convolutional downsampling tower, transformer core, deconvolutional upsampling tower with skip connections; species conditioning by adaptive layer norms. Main models have 7 downsamples; experimental models have 5. The second-generation checkpoints use a different architecture.
facts.source_locator: docs at commit 2dc37b86: Architecture, Ablations; current docs: opening note

quotes.text: NTv3 employs a U-Net-like architecture optimized for long-range genomic modeling:
7 downsamples require sequence length divisible by 128; 5 downsamples require divisible by 32
Those checkpoints use a different architecture

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA, one token per base (A, T, C, G, N plus special tokens). Length must be divisible by 128 (7-downsample models) or 32 (5-downsample models); pad with N, not [PAD]. Post-trained models also take a species name.
facts.source_locator: docs at commit 2dc37b86: Tokenization, Sequence Length Requirements, How to Use

quotes.text: or pad them with `N` tokens to the nearest valid length. **The models however were not trained on [PAD] tokens**

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Pre-trained: masked-token logits and embeddings from chosen layers. Post-trained: full-length language model logits, plus BigWig functional track predictions and BED genome annotation predictions over the middle 37.5% of the input.

run_guide.summary: Install the nucleotide-transformer package at the initial-release commit and run the documented example that loads NTv3_100M_post and predicts tracks and annotations for two 32,768-base sequences.
prerequisites: Python with venv and pip, and git. Use a separate environment from any install of the current code.
Access to the gated NTv3_100M_post repository on Hugging Face (the API reports automatic approval), then huggingface-cli login.
The weights are for non-commercial use only under the InstaDeep Open Model Licence, and the code is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
The code runs on GPU and TPU through JAX. Memory needs are not stated.

steps.title: Run the post-trained model
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import jax.numpy as jnp
from nucleotide_transformer_v3.pretrained import get_posttrained_ntv3_model

# Get post-trained model
posttrained_model, tokenizer, config = get_posttrained_ntv3_model(
    model_name="NTv3_100M_post",
)

# Get data and tokenize it - 2 sequences of length 2**15 (32768 nucleotides)
seq_length = 2**15  # 32768
sequences = ["A" * seq_length, "T" * seq_length]  # 2 sequences
tokens = tokenizer.batch_np_tokenize(sequences)

# Get species token from conditions vocabulary
species = 'human'
species_tokens = posttrained_model.encode_species(species)

outs = posttrained_model(
    tokens=tokens,
    species_tokens=species_tokens,
)

logits = outs["logits"]
bigwig_logits = outs["bigwig_tracks_logits"]
bed_logits = outs["bed_tracks_logits"]

print(f"logits shape: {logits.shape}")  # Full sequence length
print(f"bigwig_logits shape: {bigwig_logits.shape}")  # Cropped to middle 37.5%
print(f"bed_logits shape: {bed_logits.shape}")  # Cropped to middle 37.5%
PY
